newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers' talks suspended till 1500 GMT.
newsitem.headline: French truckers' talks suspended till 1500 GMT.

text.p: Truck drivers' unions, employers and a government mediator suspended talks on ending a 10-day-old dispute strangling French roads on Wednesday morning after a marathon 20-hour session and will reconvene at 4 p.m. (1500 GMT), negotiators said.
Roger Poletti of the Force Ouvriere union told reporters: "Things have moved forward." But he said some 200 roadblocks around the country would remain in place.

Transport Minister Bernard Pons told reporters after the weekly cabinet meeting he was "neither optimistic nor pessimistic but realistic", saying considerable progress had been made but several points remained to be solved.
Unions said a consensus had been reached on allowing drivers with 25 years' service to retire at 55 instead of 60 on 75 percent of their salary, subject to an overall deal..
But Marc Blondel, FO's general secretary, said employers must agree to pay drivers for loading time and compulsory rest periods on the road if the dispute was to be settled.
The drivers, who have blocked highways, borders and fuel depots, causing petrol shortages in several regions, are also demanding a 10 percent pay rise and shorter working hours.
